theater: 伊比利亞塔霍河上游山地

battle.name: 盧西坦戰爭
battle.theater: 伊比利亞塔霍河上游山地
battle.brief: 公元前154年起，羅馬共和國三次派兵深入伊比利亞塔霍河上游山地，鎮壓由維里阿圖斯率領的盧西坦聯盟，先後折損多名將領，最終由加利巴於前138年收尾。卡面這件斯巴達長矛並未現身戰場，它留下的是希臘方陣刺擊長矛的樣式譜系，羅馬軍團的短刺與重投槍出自同一條工藝路線。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 交戰的兩方是羅馬共和國與伊比利亞半島上以盧西坦人為核心的部落聯盟。羅馬方面的決策在元老院，兵權逐任交給執政官：公元前150年由執政官昆圖斯·法比奧斯·馬西莫斯·阿米利亞努斯領兵，結果連戰皆北；公元前149年改由執政官普布利奧斯·科爾涅利奧·西庇阿·艾米利亞努斯接任總指揮，兩名執政官級副將協同作戰。輔助步兵由義大利各城鎮與拉丁盟邦徵集，騎兵來自羅馬殖民地、小亞細亞的希臘城邦以及西班牙的盟邦城市，後勤靠船隊自地中海把糧秣運到塔霍河口，再以獸車轉入內陸山路。盧西坦一方並非國家，而是盧西坦人吸納維拉泰諾人、卡雷塔尼人等山地部族形成的聯盟，重大行動由部落會議推舉一位最高統帥，維里阿圖斯即以此身份當選。聯軍以投槍手與持矛步兵為主力，另有輕裝騎兵，波利比烏斯記其兵力約為二萬步兵與五千騎兵。雙方都無須爭奪海權，戰事重心全落在陸路推進、渡河點與山區堡壘的爭奪上。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Roman Republic and a tribal alliance in the Iberian Peninsula built around the Lusitanians. On the Roman side, the Senate made the decisions and the command passed from consul to consul: Quintus Fabius Maximus Aemilianus led the campaign of 150 BC and was defeated twice, and in 149 BC the overall command was handed to the consul Publius Cornelius Scipio Aemilianus, assisted by two legates of consular rank. Auxiliary infantry was levied from the towns of Italy and the Latin League, cavalry came from the Roman colonies, the Greek cities of Asia Minor and the Spanish allied communities, and supplies were carried by sea to the mouth of the Tagus and then moved inland on pack animals and carts along the mountain tracks. The Lusitanian side was not a state but a coalition formed by the Lusitani together with mountain peoples such as the Vettones and the Carpetani, and for major operations a council of the tribes elected a single supreme commander; Viriathus held that office by such an election. The coalition fought with javelin skirmishers and spear-armed infantry supported by light cavalry, and Polybius puts its strength at roughly 20,000 foot and 5,000 horse. Neither side needed command of the sea: the war was fought entirely over land routes, river crossings and hill forts.
people: 維里阿圖斯是全場的核心人物。他是盧西坦人，出身科瓦·達·莫拉一帶的部落，公元前2世紀初推翻迦太基人的徵募統治後被推舉為統帥，此後七年以山區為根據地，組織游擊、襲擊羅馬縱隊與營地，並在公元前148年的大敗之後仍能重整隊伍再戰。羅馬方面的關鍵人物是普布利奧斯·科爾涅利奧·西庇阿·艾米利亞努斯，即後來摧毀迦太基的小西庇阿；他於公元前149年以代執政官身分接任戰場指揮，以冬營、斷糧與追擊把速戰速決的期望拖成消耗戰。有一個被反覆引用的細節：西庇阿的幼子在前146年的一次夜襲中被俘，維里阿圖斯不但把人放回，還派信使帶話譏諷這位羅馬將領，此事見於波利比烏斯與阿庇安的記載。首任主將法比奧斯在公元前150年連失兩陣，公元前151年隨軍的執政官埃米利奧·萊皮達斯更在軍營中病逝，疫病與士氣成了這支部隊的另一名敵人。公元前140年執政官塞爾維利奧·凱皮奧在塔霍河下游接戰，公元前138年由執政官塞爾維烏斯·蘇爾皮基奧·加利巴收尾；加利巴早年在西庇阿麾下當過軍務官，深知盧西坦戰法的破綻在哪裡。
peopleEn: Viriathus is the central figure of the whole war. He was a Lusitanian from the tribes around Cova da Moura, and after the revolt that broke the power of the Carthaginian recruiting officers at the beginning of the second century BC he was elected commander by his own people. For the next seven years he used the highlands as his base, organizing skirmishes, raiding Roman columns and camps, and after the heavy defeat of 148 BC he was still able to reform his force and fight again. The key Roman figure was Publius Cornelius Scipio Aemilianus, the younger Scipio who would later destroy Carthage; he took over the command in 149 BC as proconsul and turned a war of quick decision into a war of attrition through winter camps, cutting supplies and pursuit. One much-quoted detail: the young son of Scipio was taken prisoner in a night raid of 146 BC, and Viriathus not only released him but sent a messenger with a message mocking the Roman general, a story preserved by both Polybius and Appian. The first commander, Fabius, lost two engagements in 150 BC, and the consul Aemilius Lepidus who accompanied the campaign in 151 BC died of illness in camp, so disease and morale became enemies in their own right. The consul Quintus Servilius Caepio took over the fighting along the lower Tagus in 140 BC, and the war was closed out in 138 BC by the consul Servius Sulpicius Galba, who had earlier served as a military tribune under Scipio and knew exactly where the Lusitanian way of war was brittle.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛並沒有出現在伊比利亞的戰場上。它是公元前8世紀希臘重裝步兵方陣的標誌：兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套，槍首是青銅的三角矛尖。它之所以值得放在這場戰爭的卡面，是因為它標示了刺擊長矛樣式譜系的起點，而真正在塔霍河上游揮動的是雙方各自的刺擊與投擲武器。羅馬方面使用長約兩公尺、末端帶尖鐵的重投槍皮魯姆，以及第三線裝備的短刺，配以西班牙式短劍、圓盾、鎖子甲與頭盔；盧西坦人裝備輕得多，以長矛配合標槍射擊作戰，輔以伊比利亞式彎刀 falcata 與小型圓盾，騎兵不備鞍具，靠毯子與皮帶控制坐騎，與狄奧多羅斯對伊比利亞騎兵的描述相符。攻城與後勤器械方面，羅軍攜帶帳幕工兵、攻城槌、雲梯、柴車與攻城塔，並以水陸兩用的輜重獸隊維持供給；盧西坦一方沒有攻城能力，全靠山寨、峭壁與井泉作為抵抗的依托。有趣的是，羅馬裝備與希臘方陣的長矛共享同一條工藝路線：同一根木桿，一端是負責刺穿的尖端，另一端是配重的銅套或鐵箍，卡面那句槍尾帶銅套，說的正是這枚配重件在刺擊兵器上的作用——它讓長矛在撞上盾牌時不易脫手。
kitsEn: The dory on the card never fought in Iberia. It is the emblem of the Greek heavy infantry phalanx of the eighth century BC: a two-metre wooden shaft with a bronze butt-spike and a bronze triangular head. It earns a place on this card because it marks the beginning of the stylistic lineage of the thrusting spear, and what actually swung along the upper Tagus were the thrusting and throwing weapons of the two sides. The Romans used the heavy javelin known as the pilum, about two metres long with an iron point, together with the short thrusting spear carried in the third line, supported by the Spanish gladius, round shields, chain mail and helmets. The Lusitanians were far more lightly equipped, fighting with spears and javelins thrown at range and using the Iberian falcata and small round shields; their horsemen rode without a saddle, controlling the horse with a blanket and straps, exactly as Diodorus describes the Iberian cavalry. On the siege and logistics side, the Roman column carried engineers' shelters, battering rams, ladders, vineae and towers, and kept itself supplied by pack animals and wagons on roads usable by both. The Lusitanians had no siege capability at all and relied on hill forts, cliffs and springs as the basis of their resistance. What links the Roman equipment to the Greek phalanx spear is a shared craft tradition: the same wooden shaft, with a piercing head at one end and a weighted bronze or iron cap at the other, and that butt-spike named on the card is precisely the counterweight that kept the spear from twisting out of the hand when it struck a shield.
tactics: 羅馬的戰術是這場戰爭的主軸。艾米利亞努斯沿用三線縱隊的步兵配置：青年兵、主力兵與老兵三列以百人隊為單位交替推進，前列以皮魯姆齊射壓住對手再後撤掩蔽，縱隊配置本身就是從希臘方陣演變而來的產物；弓箭手與盟邦輔助步兵配置於兩翼，騎兵負責襲擾與側翼反衝。羅馬刻意避免在不利地形與盧西坦人正面交鋒，改以冬營為據：壕溝、夯土牆與柵欄構成的營地既是宿營也是堡壘，冬春兩季以搜索隊巡邏、摧毀田禾、切斷水源，逼迫對手飢餓，公元前149年元老院還把戰爭定性為不義之戰，藉以穩固軍心與盟邦的向背。波利比烏斯記載的決定性手法是一場有計畫的撤退：羅馬以全線後撤誘使盧西坦人追出陣地，拉散其縱隊後再以整齊後備與兩翼騎兵回身反擊，會戰遂以對方崩潰告終。盧西坦人則以游擊與地形抵抗：結陣時以標槍齊射削弱敵軍前排，再以輕騎反覆襲擾羅馬縱隊與糧車，避免與兩軍團正面交鋒，並在夜間突襲羅馬營地奪取輜重。其弱點也很明確：沒有後備、沒有攻城器械，一擊不中便難以重整，聯盟盟邦一旦被離間，陣腳立刻鬆動。
tacticsEn: Roman tactics form the backbone of this war. Aemilianus used the three-line infantry order: hastati, principes and triarii in centuries alternating forward, the front rank loosing a volley of pila to pin the enemy and then withdrawing behind cover, a deployment that was itself a product of the evolution from the Greek phalanx. Archers and allied auxiliaries were posted on the flanks, and cavalry handled harassment and counter-charge. The Romans deliberately refused to meet the Lusitanians in the open on ground of their own choosing, and instead made winter camps their instrument: ditches, rammed-earth walls and palisades made the camp both quarters and fortress, while through winter and spring scouting parties burned crops and cut off water to force the enemy to starve. In 149 BC the Senate even declared the war a bellum iniustum, an unjust war, in order to steady the troops and to hold the loyalty of the allies. The decisive device recorded by Polybius is a planned retreat: the Roman line withdrew in good order to draw the Lusitanians out of their formation and stretch them out, and then turned with fresh reserves while the cavalry on both wings struck, and the battle ended in the collapse of the Lusitanian line. The Lusitanians in turn fought a war of skirmish and terrain: they opened with massed javelins to weaken the enemy front, harried Roman columns and baggage trains with light horse, avoided meeting the two legions in a set-piece engagement, and struck Roman camps at night to carry off equipment. Their weaknesses were just as clear: no reserves, no siege train, no ability to regroup after a failed stroke, and the moment one allied tribe was detached from the coalition the whole formation loosened.
data: 可核對的數字主要來自波利比烏斯與阿庇安兩家記載，兩家在若干處並不一致，引用時須保留餘地。時間上，戰爭自公元前154年或前153年盧西坦人襲擊羅馬盟邦起，至公元前138年加利巴取得最後勝利為止，前後約十七年，其間有三次大規模進攻：前150年法比奧斯的敗績、前149至前148年艾米利亞努斯的戰役、前140至前138年凱皮奧與加利巴的收尾戰。兵力方面，波利比烏斯記盧西坦聯軍約二萬步兵、五千騎兵；羅軍由兩個軍團（每團約四千人、三百騎兵）加上盟邦輔助部隊組成，輔助步兵約二萬、輔助騎兵約二千，兩種解讀都有人主張，合計落在三萬上下。公元前149年元老院另決議增派約二千名步兵，騎兵由殖民地提供，亞細亞的希臘城邦也派來援軍。會戰規模與傷亡數字在古代記錄中並不可靠：波利比烏斯只說羅軍損失甚微而盧西坦軍被大量俘虜，阿庇安同樣沒有留下可信的陣亡數，因此不宜引用任何精確數字。地理上，羅軍自埃布羅河下游的行省據點出發，渡過塔霍河後進入今葡萄牙北部的高地，最後的堡壘在科瓦·達·莫拉一帶的山中，後世一般認為在今米蘭達杜多羅附近，最後一段推進以百餘公里計。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked come mainly from Polybius and Appian, and the two do not agree everywhere, so their numbers have to be used with caution. In time, the war runs from 154 or 153 BC, when the Lusitanians attacked Roman allies, to 138 BC, when Galba won the last engagement, roughly seventeen years in all and three large Roman offensives: the failed campaign of Fabius in 150 BC, the war of Aemilianus from 149 to 148 BC, and the closing campaigns of Caepio and Galba from 140 to 138 BC. On numbers of men, Polybius gives the Lusitanian coalition about 20,000 foot and 5,000 horse; the Roman force was two legions of about 4,000 foot and 300 horse each, together with allied auxiliaries of roughly 20,000 foot and 2,000 horse, a figure that admits two readings and totals somewhere near 30,000. In 149 BC the Senate voted a reinforcement of about 2,000 infantry, with cavalry provided by the colonies and further troops from the Greek cities of Asia. Casualty figures for the pitched battle cannot be trusted: Polybius says only that the Roman losses were slight and that large numbers of Lusitanians were taken prisoner, and Appian leaves no credible death toll either, so no precise number should be quoted. Geographically, the Roman column set out from the provincial base near the lower Ebro, crossed the Tagus and climbed into the highlands of modern northern Portugal, and the last stronghold lay in the mountains around Cova da Moura, generally placed near Miranda do Douro; the final stage of the advance is measured in a little over a hundred kilometres.
cause: 戰爭的直接導火線，是羅馬在西班牙的官署介入地方糾紛。第二次布匿戰爭後，羅馬在伊比利亞建立兩個行省，山地各部落表面臣服，地方事務卻由羅馬的財政代理與代執政官實際裁決。據阿庇安記載，盧西坦人內部一份首領之位與隨之而來的產業出現繼承爭端，羅馬官員偏袒其中有錢的一方，另一方因此被殺，盧西坦人殺死涉事者以求解，羅馬要求交出兇手而遭拒絕。公元前154年元老院派出三人代表團前往調查，代表團在部落間居留並學習當地語言，此舉加深了雙方的對立。更深的背景是迦太基的退場：第二次布匿戰爭期間，迦太基在伊比利亞徵召的盧西坦傭兵約二千人，於公元前212年在塞爾提比里亞人卡魯斯率領下倒戈，擊潰哈米爾卡·巴卡的軍隊並迫使其敗亡，此後盧西坦人持續以掠奪與劫持人質向羅馬施壓。最終選擇開戰的是羅馬一方：公元前153年盧西坦人進攻羅馬盟友卡雷塔尼與瓦卡埃人並取得大勝，公元前151年兩位執政官開赴戰場，卻在糧秣、疫病與地形上連遭挫折，到公元前150年元老院已把這場戰爭定性為不義之戰，兵援與指揮權隨即交到艾米利亞努斯手上。
causeEn: The immediate spark was the interference of Roman officials in local disputes. After the Second Punic War Rome had established two provinces in Iberia; the mountain tribes submitted outwardly, but local affairs were in practice decided by the Roman financial agents and propraetors. According to Appian, a dispute over the succession to a local command and the property that went with it arose among the Lusitanians, the Roman official favoured the wealthy claimant, the other was killed, the Lusitanians killed the man involved to settle the score, and when Rome demanded the culprits and was refused, the matter was carried to the Senate. In 154 BC the Senate sent a commission of three to investigate; the envoys lived among the tribes and learned their language, and the episode deepened the mistrust on both sides. The deeper background is the departure of Carthage: the roughly 2,000 Lusitanian mercenaries that Carthage recruited in Iberia during the Second Punic War revolted in 212 BC under a Celtiberian named Carus, beat the army of Hamilcar Barca and forced his ruin, and from then on the Lusitanians kept up pressure on Rome through raids and the taking of hostages. The decision to open war was Rome's: in 153 BC the Lusitanians struck the Roman allies, the Carpetani and Vaccaei, and won a great victory; two consuls went out in 151 BC and were successively frustrated by supplies, disease and terrain; by 150 BC the Senate had already declared the war an unjust war, and the reinforcements and the command passed to Aemilianus.
impact: 這場十七年的戰爭改變了伊比利亞的權力結構。盧西坦聯盟從此失去獨立的統戰機構，山地部落被拆散，編入羅馬的稅制與屯駐體系；塔霍河上游第一次被常備軍團長期控制，羅馬的西班牙邊界由內陸高原推到塔霍河與其支流一帶，前2世紀中葉通往大西洋沿岸的陸路與海路通道因此打開。戰爭留下兩項長久影響，都被後世反覆引用：一是冬季戰役的示範，羅馬以冬營、斷糧、離間敵方盟邦與長期屯駐取代一次會戰定勝負的模式，此後對凱爾提貝利亞與對高盧的戰爭都沿用這套辦法；二是維里阿圖斯本人成為反羅馬的象徵，十五世紀葡萄牙的起義者費利佩·德·法爾塔萊斯以他的名字號召，兵敗被殺後頭顱被掛在埃武拉的城門上，直到今日伊比利亞多地仍以維里阿圖斯為地方榮譽的名號。對羅馬內部而言，這場戰爭也證明了元老院可以把海外戰爭升格為帝國事業，並且在將軍與元老院之間反覆角力，最終開啟了西庇阿·阿非利加那一系在西班牙的長期經營。
impactEn: This seventeen-year war changed the balance of power in Iberia. The Lusitanian coalition lost its independent war-making institution for good; the mountain tribes were broken up and drawn into the Roman tax and garrison system; the upper Tagus was for the first time held permanently by Roman legions, and the Roman frontier in Spain moved from the inland plateau down to the Tagus and its tributaries, opening the land and sea routes to the Atlantic coast in the middle of the second century BC. Two consequences were cited again and again. The first was the demonstration of the winter campaign: a pattern in which winter camps, cutting of supplies, detaching an enemy from his allies and long-term garrison duty replaced a single decisive battle, and this pattern was used again in the wars against the Celtiberians and the Gauls. The second was Viriathus himself, who became the symbol of resistance to Rome; the Portuguese rebel of the fifteenth century, Felipe de Fartailez, took his name, and after his defeat his head was hung on the gates of Evora, while towns across Iberia still carry the name of Viriathus as a mark of local honour. Inside Rome the war also showed that the Senate could raise an overseas conflict to the status of a cause of the empire, and that the struggle between general and Senate opened the long Iberian command of the line of Scipio Africanus.
result: 公元前148年的會戰之後，戰爭並未立刻結束。維里阿圖斯退入山區堡壘，重整殘部繼續抗戰，盧西坦人把作戰轉為長期游擊；羅軍則在圍困中切斷堡壘周邊的水源與田地。據阿庇安記載，前146年維里阿圖斯寧可讓侍衛將自己刺死，也不願被羅馬人擒獲，屍首被送回部眾，隨後盧西坦人接受投降，戰鬥至此才以部族解體的形式收場。剩餘的戰事由執政官塞爾維利奧·凱皮奧在公元前140至前139年於塔霍河下游接手，他擊潰尚存的盧西坦主力。最後由執政官塞爾維烏斯·蘇爾皮基奧·加利巴在公元前138年完成收尾：他利用盟邦凱爾提貝利亞人的動搖，謊稱大軍即將渡河，使盧西坦聯軍被側翼打散；盧西坦人曾在夜襲中攻佔羅馬營地，加利巴隨後以設於高地的新營與搜索行動反轉局面，奪回營帳與掠物，逼得殘部放棄自己的營壘、接受談判。戰爭以盧西坦聯盟瓦解、領袖死亡、部隊被解體或收編告終；羅馬換來對塔霍河上游的長期控制，但同時也暴露出一個問題：西班牙的邊界並未因這場勝利而關上，反而成了下一階段高盧戰爭的前沿。
resultEn: The war did not end with the battle of 148 BC. Viriathus withdrew into a mountain fortress, reformed his remnants and went on fighting, and the Lusitanians turned the conflict into a long war of skirmish; the Roman army answered by blockade, cutting the water and the fields around the fortress. According to Appian, in 146 BC Viriathus, unable to endure being taken alive, had his guards kill him, his body was carried out to his people, and the Lusitanians then accepted the terms of surrender, so that the fighting closed with the dissolution of the tribes rather than with an ordinary peace. The remainder of the war was taken over by the consul Quintus Servilius Caepio in 140 and 139 BC along the lower Tagus, where he broke the surviving Lusitanian main force. The final closure came in 138 BC with the consul Servius Sulpicius Galba, who exploited the wavering Celtiberian allies by spreading the report that the Roman army was about to cross the river, so that the Lusitanian coalition was struck on its flanks; after the Lusitanians had carried off a Roman camp in a night attack, Galba reversed the situation with a new camp on high ground and aggressive scouting, recovered the tents and booty, and drove the remnants to abandon their own camp and come to terms. The war ended with the Lusitanian coalition dissolved, its leader dead, its troops disbanded or enrolled, and Rome gained lasting control of the upper Tagus, but the same victory exposed the fact that the Spanish frontier had not been closed by it; it had become the forward edge of the next stage of Gallic war.
